note: Single-pass extraction by Claude reading the paper text; evidence references sections/figures/tables. No multi-run validation.

components.description: Ref-Long benchmark motivation, design, difficulty and analyses

nodes.name: Referencing is crucial but underexplored
nodes.description: Long-context referencing, the ability to attribute items of interest to specific parts of long documents, is crucial for applications such as legal and financial work but is underexplored for long-context language models (LCLMs).

nodes.name: Existing benchmarks do not assess referencing
nodes.description: General long-context benchmarks either append irrelevant text to short tasks (unrealistic, biased) or are built from scratch with costly human annotation, while needle-in-a-haystack-style retrieval benchmarks ignore the relationship between retrieved text and its context and so are overly simple.

nodes.name: Ref-Long task definition
nodes.description: Ref-Long gives LCLMs several indexed documents containing keys and asks for the indexes of all documents that reference a specific key, emphasizing the contextual relationship between key and document over simple retrieval.

nodes.name: Ref-Long is cheap to build
nodes.description: Ref-Long tasks can be constructed cost-efficiently because only the locations of specific keys are required.

nodes.name: Three subsets from synthetic to realistic
nodes.description: Ref-Long has three subsets: Ref-Long-A (synthetic, with the template sentence 'The little penguin counted {num} stars' inserted abruptly), Ref-Long-F (natural-language keys in LLM-generated coherent news documents of about 1,000 tokens on 3 topics), and Ref-Long-Paper (citations of 47 computer-science arXiv seed papers).

nodes.name: All 13 LCLMs struggle
nodes.description: Evaluating 13 LCLMs on Ref-Long reveals significant shortcomings in long-context referencing, even for advanced models like GPT-4o.

nodes.name: Performance drops with input length
nodes.description: On Ref-Long-A, the performance of all LCLMs consistently drops as input length grows, so task difficulty increases with length.

nodes.name: No model exceeds 20% at 40K on Ref-Long-F
nodes.description: On Ref-Long-F no LCLM exceeds 20.00% exact-match accuracy at 40K-token inputs, far below claimed maximum input lengths.

nodes.name: Humans solve the tasks
nodes.description: On 50 Multi-Hard-24K tasks, two annotators gave identical correct annotations on 42 tasks and took an average of 123.95 seconds per task, while GPT-4o and o1 face significant challenges, so the tasks are manageable for humans.

nodes.name: Human strategy hints help only GPT-4o
nodes.description: Adding a human-inspired step-by-step strategy to the prompt improves GPT-4o but not weaker LCLMs, and GPT-4o remains far below human level.

nodes.name: Key format does not change conclusions
nodes.description: Replacing numeric keys with 20 fruit names does not substantially change the conclusions, so the difficulty is not an artifact of key format.

nodes.name: Long-context fine-tuning does not transfer
nodes.description: ProLong-8B-512K performs comparably to Llama-3.1-Ins-8B despite less data and a weaker backbone, while LongCite-8B underperforms its Llama-3.1-Ins-8B backbone, so models fine-tuned on other long-context tasks generalize poorly to referencing.

nodes.name: Fine-tuning on Ref-Long helps but is insufficient
nodes.description: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-Ins-8B on Multi-Easy-8K improves performance, particularly on easier tasks, but as input length and difficulty increase all models still fail, so data alone cannot overcome the limitation.

nodes.name: Paper subset also hard
nodes.description: On Ref-Long-Paper, stronger LCLMs reach only about 30% exact-match accuracy even with just 16 papers.

nodes.name: Error types by key format
nodes.description: With numeric-symbol keys (Ref-Long-A), GPT-4o rarely confuses the key with others and errs mostly by missing documents (type I, reference less); with natural-language keys it often includes documents referencing unrelated keys.

isolated_nodes.name: Referencing differs from retrieval
isolated_nodes.description: Referencing requires the model to know the location where a key appears, not merely to retrieve the key.

isolated_nodes.name: Larger models perform better
isolated_nodes.description: Models with more parameters perform better on Ref-Long-A, and Llama-3.3-Ins-70B surpasses Llama-3.1-Ins-70B.

structural_reasoning: Motivating gap in benchmarks leads to the Ref-Long task and subsets, results showing universal difficulty, and ablations ruling out human gap, prompting, key format and fine-tuning explanations.
